correctness.rationale: Uniform perimeter covariance is exactly ((2+cos(2pi/n))/6)I_2. The k=ceil(n/3) cutoff is established with strict inequalities for all n>=3; sign crossing areas and complete negative-edge sums give the displayed norm. Strict disagreement at v_k between kernels evaluated at adjacent vertices proves only vertices norm, and equality in L1-Linfinity duality classifies input extremizers. Laurent coefficients are deduced analytically for each residue class and checked independently by Sympy; direct edge integration with mpmath confirms n=3..110, but is not used as an infinite proof. No hypotheses are relaxed beyond real affine functions, regular polygons, and uniform boundary arclength.

value.rationale: The rank-three affine least-squares projector on polygonal perimeters is a canonical sharp stability problem for boundary regression. The exact all-n formula and complete optimizer locations go beyond numerical tables. The zero-crossing edges create a quantitative residue-three cubic correction, separating continuous boundary integration from both circle integration and previously known vertex-sampling Fourier projection. This nontrivial convergence mechanism makes the precise constant useful for stable polygonal approximation rather than being a gratuitous parameter slice.
